definitions.explanation: A person who is sent to run errands or do minor tasks for someone else. Often carries a negative nuance of being treated as a subordinate.
The act of going somewhere to carry out small tasks on behalf of someone else.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}の{使|つか}い{走|ばし}りをさせられた。
examples.english: I was made to run errands for my senior.

examples.japanese: いつまでも{使|つか}い{走|ばし}りの{役|やく}は{嫌|いや}だ。
examples.english: I don't want to be stuck playing the gofer forever.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}のころは{毎日|まいにち}{使|つか}い{走|ばし}りばかりだった。
examples.english: When I was new, all I did every day was run errands.

examples.japanese: ちょっと{使|つか}い{走|ばし}りを{頼|たの}まれた。
examples.english: I was asked to run a quick errand.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{走|ばし}りに{行|い}ってくる。
examples.english: I'm going to run an errand.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物|もの}の{使|つか}い{走|ばし}りで{一日|いちにち}{終|お}わった。
examples.english: The whole day was spent running shopping errands.

notes:
USAGE:
When referring to a person (sense 1), it often implies being treated as a lowly subordinate. Common in workplace and school hierarchies. Also written as {使|つか}いっ{走|ぱし}り with a geminate consonant in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}りをさせる (to make someone run errands)
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}りをさせられる (to be made to run errands)
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}りに{行|い}く (to go on an errand)
